SEMI.sells: Chips: custom AI accelerators designed for one customer each (Google's TPU and others), Ethernet switch and networking chips for AI clusters, plus non-AI chips for phones (radio and wi-fi), broadband, storage and industrial uses.
SEMI.buyers: The big cloud companies and AI labs (Google, Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI), Apple, network-equipment makers, distributors.
pos: AI chips grew +221% vs a year earlier in Q3 FY26 and are now 56% of total revenue.
Management expects about $115bn of AI revenue in FY27 vs about $58bn in FY26, with supply secured.
Customer list has widened from Google to Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI.
neg: Segment operating margin 60.7% over the last 4 quarters vs 80% in software: AI chips carry lower margins than the rest.
A handful of buyers take most AI chips; one customer moving work in-house or to a rival (e.g. Marvell's Google deal) is a direct hit.
Non-AI chips have grown slowly for years.

SW.sells: Infrastructure software, mainly VMware (software that runs companies' private clouds), plus mainframe, security and network-management software.
SW.buyers: Large companies and governments, mostly on multi-year subscriptions.
pos: Highest-margin part: 79.9% segment operating margin over the last 4 quarters vs 75.4% a year earlier.
Mostly recurring subscription revenue; recurring revenue +15% vs a year earlier in Q3 FY26.
neg: Growth swings with big contract timing: +9% in Q2 FY26, +29% in Q3 FY26 vs a year earlier.
The VMware price rises are maturing; some customers are moving to rivals such as Nutanix.
EU competition complaint by European cloud providers (CISPE, Mar 2026) over VMware licensing changes.

shift.title: VMware made it half software; AI chips are now taking it back
pos: Chips were 78.8% of revenue in the 4 quarters to Jul 2023, before VMware; software then rose to 43% a year ago; chips are back to 66.7% in the 4 quarters to Jul 2026 vs 56.8% a year earlier, driven by AI.
neg: The mix is moving towards the lower-margin part: chips' segment margin (60.7%) is 19 points below software's (79.9%), so the adjusted gross margin is falling (75.0% in Q3 FY26 vs 78.4% a year earlier; about 73% guided).
Revenue depends more each quarter on a few AI buyers' budgets and financing (chains C1, C6).

defects: Staging build, first day of history: the call needs 10 trading days of scores before it can be confirmed.

Gross margin trend (DM6) is scored before the fixed write-off of acquired intangibles (VMware) in cost of revenue, added back each quarter from Broadcom's releases (Kenneth, 24 Oct 2026); the reported (GAAP) figures are shown alongside. Stock pay and restructuring are not added back, so it is close to, not the same as, Broadcom's 'non-GAAP' margin. The engine labels these 'one-offs'; a proper adjusted-margin option is requested from the Framework chat. The engine's bearish wording ('costs rising faster than prices') is generic: here the cause is the growing share of lower-margin AI chips.
Valuation vs own history (VL3) uses trailing reported (GAAP) P/E, which carries about $8bn a year of VMware write-off, so it reads much higher than the forward P/E (VL1, analysts' adjusted EPS).

VL3's 5-year median (38.5x) is understated: the collector derives Q4 FY24 EPS as full year minus three quarters across the July 2024 10-for-1 split, giving −$5.63 instead of the reported +$0.90, which drops about a year of readings. Corrected, the median is about 46.5x and today's 42.0x is about 10% below it: still neutral (bullish needs 15% below). Same defect as NVDA; Framework fix pending.

Valuation vs peers is sensitive to the peer set: without Nutanix (pure software) the forward P/E discount narrows from 33% to about 18% (still bullish) and EV/EBITDA is about 24% above peers (bearish at 25%). Peers kept as approved (Kenneth, 24 Oct 2026).
Guidance vs expectations (DM3) uses the Reuters-wire consensus ($35.05bn); a broker figure of $34.9bn would make it neutral (Kenneth, 24 Oct 2026: keep Reuters).
AI chip revenue (DM4a) is typed in from results releases each quarter; it is not in the SEC data. Software revenue (DM4b) matches the SEC segment figure.

DM5 uses the April-June 2026 cloud capex until Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report the September quarter (28-29 Oct); Meta's September quarter (+80%) is already out. DM5 does not capture AI labs (Anthropic, OpenAI) funded by debt rather than cloud capex (see chain C6).
Chain C3 watches Micron's share price as a stand-in for memory prices; C1 watches CoreWeave as a stand-in for AI funding conditions.

Free cash flow ÷ EBITDA uses Yahoo's trailing EBITDA ($52.3bn): the engine's outlier filter drops every SEC quarter that includes amortisation (Broadcom tags it quarterly only from FY25), so the chart hover shows too-high ratios for older quarters (e.g. Jan 2024 211%) and none for the last 4. SEC-based EBITDA would be $51.4bn and the ratio 77% instead of 75%. Framework fix pending.
Cash conversion (operating cash ÷ net profit) is blank: SEC's data has no full-year FY25 net profit under the standard tag, so only one annual report is usable.

Fed rate expectations (LQ6) says odds moved 'towards cuts': the odds of a rise fell from 70% to 7% over four weeks while cut odds stayed near 0%, so markets now expect no change (engine wording; Framework chat).
Short interest (LQ2) is dated 30 Sep, Yahoo's latest; the 15 Oct report may already be out.
Chip index (^SOX) moves quoted in the text come from Yahoo Finance daily closes (25 Sep-23 Oct 2026) fetched by hand; they are not in the collector's files, so the daily refresh will not update them.
A reading exactly on a line can score on the wrong side because of rounding (e.g. forecast revisions at exactly −3.00% compute as −2.99999% and score neutral). Framework fix pending.
Chain C5 is 'Watching' (approved as Quiet): the TPU v9 report is from an analyst and is not confirmed by Google.

lead: Broadcom is Building history (today's zone: Hold), at +1 on a −100 to +100 scale: AI demand and the valuation are positive, but the price trend is fully negative, margins are slipping as AI grows, and Broadcom now lends to its own customers.
bullets: AI demand is strong; the rest is weaker. Demand scores +26: revenue grew 85.5% in the July quarter vs a year earlier, against a 31.9% average for the prior four quarters; AI chip sales +54.6% vs the April quarter (bullish line +10%); software +29.0% vs a year earlier; big-4 cloud capex about +79% vs a year earlier. Against that, gross margin before the VMware write-off was 75.5% over the last 4 quarters vs 77.0% a year earlier (−1.5 points); the October-quarter guide was 1.4 points of growth below consensus; FY27 consensus EPS is $19.43 vs $19.58 90 days ago (−0.8%).

Cheap vs peers on forecasts, not on reported profit. Valuation scores +60: 17.0x next-12-month earnings vs a 25.6x peer median (−33%); growth-adjusted P/E 0.3 vs 0.7 for the peer median (−53%); EV/EBITDA 30.7x vs 25.7x (+19%, neutral: trailing EBITDA does not yet reflect the expected growth); trailing reported P/E 42.0x vs 38.5x for its own 5-year median (+9%, neutral; the median is about 46.5x once a known data error is fixed). The discount rests on FY27 EPS rising about two-thirds and on the peer set (see Known defects).

Liquidity is slightly positive. Liquidity scores +13: the odds of a Fed rate rise fell about 61 points over four weeks (bullish); volume on up days was 0.88x volume on down days over the last 20 trading days (neutral); short interest (+7.4% vs the prior month, 1.2% of float) and fund holdings are neutral.

The price trend is broken, and not only because of the sector. Price trend scores −100: $329.17 is 10.5% below its 200-day average; the 50-day average is 3.4% below the 200-day; over 3 months it is 28.5 points behind the peers' average. On 26 Oct it rose 2.3% vs +0.7% for the S&P 500.

New risk: Broadcom finances its customers. It will lend Anthropic up to $42bn toward a $125.2bn lease of its chips, is arranging over $50bn for OpenAI's chips, and guarantees part of a $60bn+ chip-financing vehicle (chain C6). The top five end customers were about 40% of FY25 revenue. Not yet a confirmed call: day 2 of 10 on the live page. Next tests: cloud capex (28-29 Oct) and Broadcom's results (expected 9 Dec).
